helpPage.title: Help Center
helpPage.subtitle: How can we help you?
helpPage.c1Desc: Learn how the case assessment works.
helpPage.c1a1A: Answer a few quick questions about your accident. The assessment takes about 60 seconds and helps you understand if you may have a personal injury case.
helpPage.c1a2Q: Do I need to create an account?
helpPage.c1a2A: You can start the assessment without an account. Creating an account lets you save your progress, upload evidence, and track your case.
helpPage.c2a1Q: What will I learn from the assessment?
helpPage.c2a1A: You'll see if you may have a case, an estimated case value range, and typical timelines. Results are based on similar injury cases.
helpPage.c2a2A: Estimates are based on patterns from similar cases but depend on your documentation and evidence. They are for informational purposes only.
helpPage.c3Desc: How to add documents and photos.
helpPage.c3a1A: Recommended documents include: medical bills, injury photos, police reports, and wage loss documentation. The more documentation you provide, the better we can assess your case.
helpPage.c3a2A: We accept images (JPG, PNG), PDFs, and common document formats. You can upload from your computer or take photos with your phone.
helpPage.c4Desc: How we connect you with attorneys.
helpPage.c4a1A: We match your case with attorneys who specialize in your type of injury and practice in your jurisdiction. You choose when to submit your case for attorney review.
helpPage.c4a2Q: Will my case be shared automatically?
helpPage.c4a2A: No. Your case is only sent to attorneys after you approve submission. You remain in control of your information.
helpPage.c5a1A: Estimates are based on patterns from thousands of similar injury cases, including injury type, treatment, and documentation. They are not guarantees.
helpPage.c5a2A: Adding evidence, medical records, or documentation can improve the accuracy and may affect the estimated range.
helpPage.c6a1A: Yes. We use industry-standard encryption and security practices. Your data is stored securely and only shared with attorneys when you approve.
helpPage.c6a2A: Only you, until you authorize us to send your case. Then it goes to the participating law firms you selected, one at a time in the order you set, so they can decide whether to offer to represent you. Medical records are included only if you have signed a HIPAA authorization. Participating firms have commercial agreements with ClearCaseIQ for technology and marketing services; you never pay us. See our Privacy Policy for exactly what is shared and when.
helpPage.c7Desc: Need help? Reach out to us.
helpPage.c7a1A: Email support@clearcaseiq.com. Most support requests are answered within 24 hours.
helpPage.c7a2Q: Can I report a technical issue?

helpPage.guide1Body: Key factors: liability (who was at fault), injury evidence (medical records, photos), documentation (bills, reports), and damages (medical costs, lost wages).
helpPage.guide2Body: They may challenge treatment gaps, missing documentation, and inconsistent descriptions. Consistent records and complete documentation help protect your case.
helpPage.guide3Body: Attorneys consider liability (fault and causation), damages (injury severity and costs), and medical evidence (treatment records and prognosis).

aboutPage.metaDescription: ClearCaseIQ Corp. is a Los Angeles legal technology company that helps injury victims understand their options and connect with participating attorneys — with consent, not as a law firm.
aboutPage.pageIntro: ClearCaseIQ helps people injured in accidents understand their case in plain English, organize medical records, and — only if they choose — share their file with participating personal injury attorneys.
aboutPage.notLawFirm: ClearCaseIQ Corp. is a legal technology company. We are not a law firm, we do not provide legal advice, and using this platform does not create an attorney-client relationship.
aboutPage.missionBody: Too many families face injury, paperwork, and insurance pressure at once — without a clear picture of their options. We exist so people can understand a claim before they talk to a lawyer, and so attorneys receive documented, plaintiff-chosen matters instead of thin leads.
aboutPage.principleClarityBody: A free case snapshot explains strength, value range, and next steps in everyday language — without promising outcomes.
aboutPage.principleControlBody: Nothing is shared with a law firm until you authorize it, and you choose which attorneys are contacted.
aboutPage.principleHonestyBody: We disclose that we are technology, not a law firm; that estimates are informational; and that participating firms pay a flat platform fee.
aboutPage.principleCareBody: Injury and medical details are handled with privacy-minded design. Third-party marketing analytics stay off intake and signed-in screens.
aboutPage.storyBody1: ClearCaseIQ began after founder Sri Reddy's father passed away from complications following a quadruple bypass. In that moment of grief, the family did not know where to turn or how to navigate the systems around them.
aboutPage.storyBody2: That experience shaped the product: make it simple for injured people and families to share their story and documents, and make it possible for attorneys to respond with clarity and care — without burying anyone in legal jargon.
aboutPage.whatIntro: One platform serves two audiences. Consumers get clarity and control. Participating firms get intelligence and readiness — not another lead mill.

disclosures.pageIntro: How ClearCaseIQ works, what it is, and what it is not.
disclosures.aboutBody: ClearCaseIQ is an independent legal technology company. We are not a law firm and do not provide legal advice. Using this platform does not create an attorney-client relationship with ClearCaseIQ.
disclosures.attorneyNetworkBody: Attorneys displayed on the platform are independent participating law firms. ClearCaseIQ does not recommend or endorse any attorney. You decide whether to contact or retain a lawyer.
disclosures.attorneyNetworkHow: Attorneys are identified using objective criteria: the state and county of your matter, the type of claim, whether the firm handles that claim type, and how quickly the firm typically responds. You see the attorneys before anyone is contacted, you set the order in which they are contacted, and you can remove any attorney you would rather not work with. A removed attorney is not contacted and is not suggested to you again. If additional attorneys are proposed later, nothing is sent until you review that list and choose which ones to include.
disclosures.settlementBody: Settlement estimates are informational only and are not guarantees or predictions of legal outcomes. Estimates are generated from the information you provide and from comparable reported matters, and they change as documentation is added.
disclosures.participationBody: Attorneys shown here participate in the ClearCaseIQ platform. If you choose to contact or retain one of these attorneys, ClearCaseIQ may receive compensation from participating law firms for providing technology and marketing services. That fee is the same flat amount for every case. It does not change with the type or value of your claim, and it is never a share of your recovery. This does not affect your choice of attorney. You are free to choose any attorney, whether or not they participate on the platform.
disclosures.shareAuthorization: I authorize ClearCaseIQ to share my case information with the law firms I selected so they can review my case. I understand those firms have commercial agreements with ClearCaseIQ and may pay for technology and marketing services.
disclosures.shareAuthorizationRequired: Please authorize sharing your case with the firms you selected before sending it.
disclosures.howItWorksBody: ClearCaseIQ operates a legal technology platform that connects consumers with participating law firms. Participating law firms pay ClearCaseIQ for access to technology and marketing services. That is a flat fee per case, identical for every case regardless of claim type, injury severity, or expected settlement value, and it is never a percentage of any recovery. Consumers never pay ClearCaseIQ to use the platform.
disclosures.howItWorksNoInfluence: Paying to participate does not buy a better position. Attorneys are identified by the objective criteria described above, and you decide who is contacted. You are free to choose any attorney, whether or not they participate on the platform.
disclosures.aiBody: ClearCaseIQ uses automated systems, including large language models, to organize the information you provide, build a medical chronology, summarize documents, and identify participating attorneys. Rose, the platform's intake and case assistant, is an AI assistant and not a person. Automated output can be incomplete or wrong, is reviewed by people before it is acted on, and is not legal advice.
disclosures.californiaBody: If you are a California resident, the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (CCPA/CPRA) gives you the right to know what personal information we collect and how we use it, to request a copy of it, to correct it, to delete it, to limit our use of sensitive personal information, and not to be discriminated against for exercising any of those rights.
disclosures.californiaOptOut: You also have the right to opt out of the sale or sharing of your personal information. Sending your case to a participating law firm is a disclosure you authorize, and participating firms pay ClearCaseIQ a flat fee per case, so we treat that disclosure as one you can decline and withdraw. You can decline to send your case at all, remove any firm before it is contacted, or withdraw your authorization afterward from your case page. We then stop contacting firms about your case. To opt out in writing, or to make any other request under the CCPA/CPRA, email us with the subject line "California privacy request."
disclosures.californiaHow: We will verify your identity before acting on a request about your own information, and we will respond within the time the statute allows. You may use an authorized agent. Exercising these rights does not change the price or quality of anything we provide, because consumers never pay ClearCaseIQ.

value.preliminaryBody: We calculated this range from what you've shared so far. A few key figures are still missing, so treat this number as a conservative floor, not a ceiling. Adding the details below typically increases and sharpens your estimate.
value.preliminaryHint: Don't have exact numbers yet? That's normal this soon after an accident. A rough range is fine. You can refine it later as bills and records come in.
value.litigationPotentialBody: Current information suggests the case may have additional value if medical treatment continues, imaging confirms injury findings, liability evidence strengthens, or wage loss and future care are documented.
value.litigationPotentialNote: Trial outcomes are uncertain, take longer, cost more, and may be limited by collectability or policy limits.
value.baseCaseTypeBody: We start with the case category before adding facts like fault, treatment, documents, venue, insurance, and injury severity. Different claim types begin in different baseline ranges because attorneys and insurers evaluate them with different proof burdens, expected treatment patterns, and liability issues.
value.startingPointA: This is the starting point only. The displayed settlement range of
value.startingPointB: reflects later adjustments from your specific facts and available documents.
value.howBaselineBody: The model does not treat each fact as a fixed dollar add-on. Instead, it treats major facts as modifiers that can increase confidence, reduce risk discounts, move the case into a higher injury band, or keep the estimate conservative.
value.settlementCalcFormula: Injury-supported value x settlement compression x liability risk x evidence confidence x venue / insurance constraints.
value.settlementCalcNote: This is why the explanation says clear liability reduces discounting instead of saying it added a specific dollar amount.
value.trialCalcFormula: Economic damages + non-economic damages + future damages, adjusted by liability, venue, jury risk, and evidence strength.
value.calcExample: Example: clear liability usually improves confidence and reduces the fault discount. It is not modeled as a universal "+$10,000" rule because the dollar impact depends on the size of the case, injury severity, available insurance, and evidence.

calc.baselineAutoFloor: Starts in the standard personal-injury range.
calc.baselineAutoWhy: Auto cases often have clearer incident timing, insurance coverage, police reports, vehicle damage, and treatment records. The range can move up quickly when imaging, injections, surgery, commercial coverage, or serious wage loss appear.
calc.baselineAutoEx1: Soft-tissue soreness with limited treatment starts lower.
calc.baselineAutoEx2: MRI-confirmed disc injury, injections, or surgery can move the case higher.
calc.baselineAutoEx3: Clear rear-end liability and commercial coverage can materially improve review priority.
calc.baselineSlipFloor: Starts slightly lower until notice and hazard proof are clear.
calc.baselineSlipWhy: Premises cases depend heavily on proving the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. Photos, incident reports, witness statements, and medical records can move the case out of the lower baseline.
calc.baselineSlipEx1: A fall with no photos or witnesses starts cautiously.
calc.baselineSlipEx2: Fractures, surgery, or visible hazard evidence can raise the range.
calc.baselineSlipEx3: A store incident report or video preservation can improve liability confidence.
calc.baselineDogFloor: Starts higher when liability and visible injury are documented.
calc.baselineDogWhy: Dog bite cases can have strong liability rules and visible damages. Photos, scarring, infection, nerve injury, and plastic surgery recommendations can push the baseline higher.
calc.baselineDogEx1: Minor puncture wounds without scarring stay closer to the lower range.
calc.baselineDogEx2: Facial injuries, permanent scars, or child victims may increase value.
calc.baselineDogEx3: Animal-control reports and photos are especially important.
calc.baselineMedmalFloor: Starts higher, but only after expert-support risk is considered.
calc.baselineMedmalWhy: Medical malpractice matters are more expensive and harder to prove. The baseline is higher because injuries may be severe, but the case needs records, causation analysis, and often expert review before attorneys can value it confidently.
calc.baselineMedmalEx1: A poor outcome alone does not create a strong case.
calc.baselineMedmalEx2: Clear deviation from standard care plus serious harm can increase value.
calc.baselineMedmalEx3: Complete medical records and chronology are critical before attorney review.
calc.baselineNursingFloor: Starts higher when neglect, injury, and facility responsibility are documented.
calc.baselineNursingWhy: Elder-care cases often involve serious harm, vulnerable plaintiffs, regulatory issues, and facility records. The baseline depends on medical proof, staffing/fall records, photos, and whether neglect caused the injury.
calc.baselineNursingEx1: Pressure sores, falls, dehydration, or medication errors need records.
calc.baselineNursingEx2: Severe injury or death can move the case into a higher band.
calc.baselineNursingEx3: Facility charting and photos are key evidence.
calc.baselineDeathFloor: Starts in a high-severity band because the claimed harm is catastrophic.
calc.baselineDeathWhy: Wrongful death cases involve the highest damages category, but valuation still depends on liability, causation, available insurance, beneficiaries, economic losses, and supporting records.
calc.baselineDeathEx1: Clear liability and strong insurance can materially increase value.
calc.baselineDeathEx3: Beneficiary and economic-loss documentation is important.
calc.baselineProductFloor: Starts above ordinary injury cases when defect proof is plausible.
calc.baselineProductWhy: Product cases depend on proving a defective product, warnings issue, or design/manufacturing problem. The baseline grows with preserved product evidence, serious injury, similar incidents, and expert support.
calc.baselineProductEx1: Preserving the product is often critical.
calc.baselineProductEx2: Burns, fractures, surgery, or permanent harm can raise value.
calc.baselineProductEx3: Manufacturer identity and purchase records matter.
calc.baselineGenericFloor: Starts in a general personal-injury baseline until the facts are more specific.
calc.baselineGenericWhy: The system begins with a broad injury-case range, then adjusts based on liability, injury severity, treatment, evidence, venue, insurance, and missing documents.
calc.baselineGenericEx2: Objective medical proof can raise the range.
calc.baselineGenericEx3: Missing records keep the estimate conservative.
calc.liabClearerExplanation: When fault appears clearer, the model does not need to discount the case as heavily for disputed responsibility.
calc.liabMixedExplanation: When fault is partly unclear or shared fault may be argued, the model keeps more risk in the estimate.
calc.liabUnclearExplanation: When fault is hard to prove, the model treats the case more conservatively because the claim may be disputed.
calc.injHighExplanation: Serious injuries, escalation of care, surgery recommendations, or lasting impairment can move the case above the starting category range.
calc.injDocumentedExplanation: Consistent treatment makes the injury story easier to connect to the incident and reduces causation uncertainty.
calc.injGapsExplanation: Gaps in treatment can cause insurers or attorneys to question injury severity, causation, or continuity of symptoms.
calc.injEarlyExplanation: Without a clear treatment timeline, the model avoids overstating value until records, bills, or medical events are confirmed.
calc.evStrongExplanation: Police reports, medical records, bills, photos, or other supporting files make the estimate more grounded and less speculative.
calc.evGoodExplanation: The file has useful evidence, but additional records may still refine the value range.
calc.evPartialExplanation: Some evidence is available, but missing medical records, bills, photos, or liability documents may still change the estimate.
calc.evIntakeExplanation: When the case is based mostly on intake answers, the model keeps the range wider because documents have not confirmed the key facts yet.
